summary: The article profiles Paul Mitchell, the former Monaco sporting director, as a prime target for Jim Ratcliffe, who looks set to buy a 25 per cent stake in Manchester United after Sheikh Jassim withdrew. It traces Mitchell's career from MK Dons through Southampton, Tottenham and Leipzig to Monaco, noting his recruitment hits and his reported fallout with Daniel Levy. It also quotes his own blueprint for United's long-term success and suggests he may consult Ralf Rangnick before any move.
one_line: Profile of Paul Mitchell's recruitment career at MK Dons, Southampton, Tottenham, Leipzig and Monaco, and why Jim Ratcliffe may want him as Manchester United sporting director.
key_facts: Jim Ratcliffe looks set to buy a 25 per cent stake in Manchester United after fellow bidder Sheikh Jassim withdrew his offer.
talkSPORT understands Ratcliffe would take charge of footballing matters at United, which the Glazers have been accused of having little interest in.
Ratcliffe already owns OGC Nice and is planning to appoint a sporting director at United.
Paul Mitchell recently left Monaco, where he was sporting director, after earlier stints at Leipzig, Tottenham, Southampton and MK Dons.
Mitchell spotted Dele Alli after being named MK Dons head of recruitment in 2010, and joined Southampton in the same role two years later.
At Southampton his signings included Sadio Mane, Dusan Tadic, Graziano Pelle, Dejan Lovren and Victor Wanyama, earning him a move to Tottenham in 2014.

At Tottenham he signed Heung-Min Son, Toby Alderweireld, Eric Dier and Kieran Trippier, but left after less than two years from what he called his 'dream job', reportedly due to Daniel Levy's over-involvement in recruitment.

At Leipzig under Ralf Rangnick he signed Dani Olmo, Christopher Nkunku and Amadou Haidara; the club reached the 2020 Champions League semi-finals and won its first ever trophy, the DFB Pokal, in 2022.
Mitchell said Son was at the centre of criticism in his first year at Tottenham, and he defended him as a very astute finisher based on his record at Hamburg and Leverkusen.
Son was the 2022/23 Premier League top scorer.
Mitchell said United need a blueprint for the next five years, pointing to Manchester City and Liverpool as examples of long-term strategy bringing sustainable success.
Mitchell remains good friends with Rangnick and was spotted at a United youth game while Rangnick was interim coach, and he is almost certain to consult him before any Ratcliffe approach.
